title: Base-derived tensor cohomology and canonical localization comparison model
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, A and B commutative R-algebras, E=A\otimes_R B [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], Q^\bullet a cochain complex of A-modules, and D a commutative E-algebra. Use the derived categories and cohomology functors [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and extension of scalars [def-weil-module-base-change]. A base-derived tensor cohomology model consists of the total left derived functor L:D(R)\to D(B) of extension to B, its universal counit \alpha: L(Q_R)\to Q_R\otimes_R B, the ordinary complex isomorphism (Q_R\otimes_R B)\cong Q\otimes_A E sending b\otimes q to (1\otimes b)\otimes q, E-modules T_i with B-linear isomorphisms T_i\cong H^i(L(Q_R)) under which a\otimes 1 acts as H^i(L(a\cdot\mathrm{id}_{Q_R})) for every a\in A (so the E-action is the canonical one), and E-linear maps \beta_i:T_i\to H^i(Q\otimes_A E) whose restrictions to B are the counit on cohomology under these isomorphisms. It also includes the termwise E-linear map Q\otimes_A E\to Q\otimes_A D sending e\otimes q to \bar e\otimes q (the target restricted to E), and D-linear maps c_i:D\otimes_E T_i\to H^i(Q\otimes_A D) characterized by c_i(1\otimes t)=H^i(Q\otimes_A E\to Q\otimes_A D)(\beta_i(t)). Here Q_R is Q with scalars restricted to R and the A\to D map is the composite A\to E\to D. Select a model by choice from its existence theorem; T_i and c_i then denote the derived cohomology and its canonical localization comparison, with no isomorphism of \beta_i or c_i assumed.
